places.title: Stories & Places
places.subtitle: Real places in KZN preserving indigenous knowledge and heritage

items.name: KwaZulu Cultural Museum
items.desc: Located in Ulundi, this museum preserves Zulu material culture, traditional artifacts, royal history, and indigenous knowledge systems.
items.infoBoxText: Includes the Ondini site associated with the Zulu monarchy and King Cetshwayo's royal residence.

items.name: Umgungundlovu
items.desc: The reconstructed royal capital of King Dingane. Visitors can learn about governance, military organization, and traditional leadership.
items.infoBoxText: This is where many pivotal events in early Zulu kingdom history and colonial encounters took place.

items.name: eMakhosini Ophathe Heritage Park
items.desc: Known as the Valley of the Zulu Kings. It contains the graves and settlements of several early Zulu kings and ancestors of the royal family.
items.infoBoxText: The spiritual heartland preserving deep clan histories, creation traditions, and ancestral origins.

items.name: Indlondlo Cultural Village
items.desc: An interactive village where visitors learn traditional food preparation, music, dance, beadwork, family structures, and cultural practices.
items.infoBoxText: Learn directly from community members who are actively preserving these indigenous ways of life.

items.name: Veyane Cultural Village
items.desc: A community-based cultural center where visitors can experience local traditions, storytelling, crafts, and indigenous knowledge.
items.infoBoxText: A hub for oral traditions, helping keep ancestral stories alive for the next generation.

items.name: DumaZulu Traditional Village
items.desc: One of the best-known cultural villages in South Africa, offering demonstrations of beadwork, basket weaving, shield making, and pottery.
items.infoBoxText: Features extensive traditional healing (sangoma) demonstrations, alongside music and dance.

items.name: Isandlwana Battlefield
items.desc: One of the most important battlefields in African history, where the Zulu regiments outmaneuvered British forces in 1879.
items.infoBoxText: Indigenous oral traditions and military knowledge (amabutho formations) remain central to understanding the battle.

items.name: Rorke's Drift
items.desc: Closely connected to the Anglo-Zulu War, preserving the stories of the Zulu kingdom’s military encounters.
items.infoBoxText: A site of intense historical significance directly tied to the aftermath of Isandlwana.

items.name: Spioenkop Battlefield
items.desc: A historic battlefield where guides often discuss indigenous perspectives on conflict, leadership, and survival in the region.
items.infoBoxText: Overlooks vast landscapes carrying deep histories of intersecting cultures and warfare.

items.name: Talana Museum
items.desc: Contains exhibits on Zulu history, archaeology, traditional lifestyles, and regional heritage in the Dundee area.
items.infoBoxText: A comprehensive look at the coal mining history and indigenous populations of northern KZN.

items.name: Maloti-Drakensberg Park
items.desc: Home to ancient San rock art and centuries of indigenous knowledge about plants, animals, weather, and mountain survival.
items.infoBoxText: A UNESCO World Heritage site preserving deep ancestral connections and indigenous astronomy.

items.name: Ngoye Forest
items.desc: One of South Africa's oldest indigenous forests. Local communities associate it with traditional stories and medicinal plants.
items.infoBoxText: A vital ecosystem for harvesting traditional medicines (amakhambi) and observing sacred natural sites.

items.name: iSimangaliso Wetland Park
items.desc: Local communities have long used traditional ecological knowledge to understand fishing, harvesting, wildlife, and conservation here.
items.infoBoxText: Demonstrates centuries of sustainable living and indigenous interaction with marine environments.

items.name: mNweni Cultural & Hiking Centre
items.desc: Offers community-guided experiences where visitors learn about mountain traditions, indigenous plant knowledge, and local history.
items.infoBoxText: A powerful example of community-led tourism celebrating traditional farming and livestock practices.

items.name: Kwa Muhle Museum
items.desc: Provides insight into the modern social history of KwaZulu-Natal and the experiences of local communities.
items.infoBoxText: Explores the cultural interactions between indigenous African communities and urban development.
